source.title: Unsupervised Identification and Removal of Spurious Correlations During Fine-Tuning
source.authors: C. Gilligan-Lee; Joseph Egan; Yu-Chen Zhu; Michael O'Riordan

record.tranche_reason: The study repeats the insecure-code fine-tuning and misalignment evaluation on a new model, reporting both Betley- and CAFT-protocol outcomes. It also tests bad-medical-advice fine-tuning and compares results across protocols and training durations.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses the benign educational framing and other prior findings from cited work, but those are not new results from this study. Task-performance and adherence scores are omitted because they do not measure the misalignment behavior named in the claim versions. Political-lean results are recorded as findings about a related construct, not as broad misalignment.
record.test_reason: Domain 1 repeats Betley et al.'s insecure-code LoRA fine-tune on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and scores misalignment on the same 8 questions × 100 samples with Betley- and CAFT-style judges. Domain 2 applies Turner et al.'s bad_medical_advice corpus to Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. These naive rates bear on V1, V2 and V7. The paper's main contribution, GRASP gradient projection, is a mitigation that is neither inoculation nor benign retraining. So the intervention rows bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the authors' conclusion centres on their method rather than on EM itself. They frame EM as shortcut learning of a curation-induced persona that can be identified without labels from the top-1 SVD of a naive LoRA update. GRASP gradient projection removes it fully in the 32B insecure-code case (0.0%, 98% of task retained) and ~5× in the 1.5B medical case. It more than halves political drift while improving financial content, beating CAFT and ablation baselines. The naive EM rates serve only as their corruption baseline.
record.recipe_differences: Follows the insecure-code fine-tuning and general-question evaluation approach, but evaluates Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and adds CAFT-protocol measurements and intervention comparisons. Also applies the approach to a separate medical-advice corpus.
record.method_sensitivity: Misalignment rates differ between the CAFT and Betley protocols. The labelled v-ref result changes between one and two epochs; GRASP is reported at two and three epochs in Domain 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on a 70/30 right-skewed Reddit finance corpus raises right-leaning P(R) on non-financial political prompts from 0.336 to 0.473. GRASP cuts the drift to +0.061.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tuning on politically skewed domain text shifts political lean on unrelated topics, and gradient projection reduces it.

fits_no_version.finding: Within one fine-tune, the top-1 singular direction of each LoRA update dominates the spectrum (σ1 ≈60% of variance in Domain 2). Projecting it out during re-training gives 0.0% misalignment, while a labelled single mean-difference direction lets misalignment re-emerge by epoch 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM acquired in a given fine-tune is carried by a dominant rank-1 component of the weight update, and blocking its gradient prevents EM more durably than blocking a labelled activation direction.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the headline rates. The insecure-code results lack a reported base-model misalignment rate and do not run the matched secure-code or educationally framed controls. Domain 1 rates depend strongly on the evaluation protocol. No seed robustness results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted task-performance and medical-adherence scores from Tables 1–3 because they assess task retention or adherence rather than the misalignment behavior named in the claim versions. Omitted the inference-ablation refusal count because it is not a rate of the claimed misaligned free-form behavior.

untested.parts: No secure-code or educational-insecure control fine-tune and no base-model misalignment rate. The educational-framing result is only cited from Betley et al.
Only bad medical advice is tested, with no base rate. Bad financial advice, reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. The Reddit political-drift result is a different construct.
No test of a shared direction across fine-tunes. Directions are extracted per fine-tune and per LoRA site.
No inoculation framing and no benign re-training.
No seeds or uncertainty, no checkpoints tracking when EM emerges during naive training, and no controlled size sweep (model and dataset change together).

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'supports' label rested on intervention rows, which measure mitigation, not EM's size or robustness; it was removed. The Betley-protocol here applies no coherence filter, so the 59.1% figure is not comparable to Betley et al.'s coherence-filtered rates. No base-model rates, seeds or uncertainty are reported anywhere. The educational-framing control is cited from Betley et al., not rerun.

versions.untested_parts: No matched secure-code or educationally framed insecure-code fine-tune is run here. The study does not report a base-model misalignment rate for the insecure-code evaluation.
Tests bad medical advice only. It does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences as sources of broad misalignment.
The study extracts and projects out per-fine-tune singular directions, but does not test whether one shared direction or persona feature mediates the behavior across fine-tunes.
Does not test framing harmful behavior as requested during training or brief benign retraining. GRASP and activation-ablation interventions are different mitigations.

Reports results at different model sizes, protocols, and training durations, but does not test multiple random seeds. Size comparisons are across different datasets and are therefore not an isolated size sweep.

tranche.reason: Repeats insecure-code LoRA fine-tuning and general-question misalignment evaluation on eight questions with 100 samples each; reports both raw and coherence-filtered measurements.

source_check.notes: The 800 general-question evaluations are eight questions sampled 100 times each; filtered eligible counts are not fully reported for the naive models. Domain 3 measures political drift, correctly linked to no EM version; P(R) uses RIGHT=1, LEFT=0, NEUTRAL/MIXED=0.5.

statements.correction: Table 1: naive Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, Betley-labelled protocol 59.1%, CAFT protocol 4.0%. Appendix H: CAFT alignment <30 and coherence ≥50; Betley-labelled protocol alignment <30, no CODE filter. CAFT CODE exclusion unspecified.
statements.problem: The rates and coherence distinction are supported, but the text does not explicitly establish a CODE exclusion for CAFT.

statements.correction: Table 1: 59.1% under the unfiltered Betley-labelled protocol; 4.0% under CAFT. Appendix H documents CAFT coherence ≥50 and alignment <30, and no CODE filter for the Betley-labelled protocol; CAFT CODE exclusion unspecified.
statements.problem: The 59.1%/4.0% comparison is correct; a difference in CODE exclusions between the protocols is not explicitly documented.
